prompt: Distinguish between distance and displacement in terms of scalar and vector definitions.

answer.text: Distance is a scalar quantity that has magnitude only (the total length of the path travelled). Displacement is a vector quantity that has magnitude and direction (the straight-line change in position from the starting point to the finishing point).

response_structure.guidance: Explicitly identify which is scalar and which is vector, and mention direction.

mark_scheme: 1 mark: Distance is a scalar / has magnitude only.
1 mark: Displacement is a vector / has magnitude and direction.
hints: Name the category (scalar or vector) for each.
Mention magnitude and direction for displacement.
solution: Distance is a scalar quantity having magnitude only. Displacement is a vector quantity having both magnitude and direction.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Identify distance as scalar (magnitude only) (1 mark).
Step 2: Identify displacement as vector (magnitude and direction) (1 mark).
lesson_anchors: A scalar is complete without a direction
A vector needs a direction as well
exclusions: vector addition and resolution deferred to l11
